raw_response:
I farm just 10.1 mu, so I cannot take big risks. We have seven people in the family, but some go out to work, so at the busy time I still mainly count on the people at home and sometimes ask for a little help. Same as before, I will keep wheat and maize on the land. This way is steady here in Quzhou. Wheat gives us a sure harvest, and maize follows right after, so even if one side is not perfect, the whole year still has some income. I cannot read the fancy recommendations, so I mostly do what has worked on my own fields and what the neighbors around me do. If the wheat seedlings look weak, I will give a bit more fertilizer, because I am more afraid of losing yield than spending a little extra. But money is still tight, and well water costs money too, so I will not overdo it. For wheat, I will sow in early October, put fertilizer before sowing, then topdress once when it starts growing strongly in spring. I will water a few times if rain is short. After wheat harvest in June, I will hurry to plant maize right away, with simple field preparation so I do not miss the season. Maize usually needs less water than wheat, so I will watch the rain and only irrigate if it is too dry. I do not plan fancy changes this year, just a steady way that protects yield and does not spend too much cash.
